source.title: HITRUST CSF v11.3
source.legalReference: HITRUST CSF v11.3 (based on ISO 27001, NIST, HIPAA)

strategies.name: Information Protection Program (01.x)
strategies.description: Governance controls that establish and maintain an information protection program. Covers organizational security policies, access reviews, privileged identity management, authentication methods, and identity provider configuration.

ML1.summary: Establish identity governance foundations: configure Entra ID tenant security defaults, enable self-service password reset, deploy access reviews, and define allowed authentication methods to eliminate weak authenticators.

ML2.summary: Strengthen identity governance: enable privileged identity management, enforce SSPR registration, deploy password protection with custom banned lists, and configure external collaboration settings.

ML3.summary: Implement advanced identity controls: enforce token protection to bind tokens to specific devices, and restrict external access governance with granular domain-level controls.

strategies.name: Access Control (02.x)
strategies.description: Controls that manage who can access organizational systems, data, and resources. Covers conditional access policies, multi-factor authentication, risk-based access, device enrollment restrictions, and passwordless authentication.

ML1.summary: Establish foundational access controls: block legacy authentication, enforce MFA for all users, and require MFA for administrative roles to prevent credential-based attacks.

ML2.summary: Enforce risk-based and conditional access: require device compliance for access, deploy sign-in and user risk policies, and restrict access based on location and platform conditions.

ML3.summary: Implement advanced access controls: deploy Windows Hello for Business for passwordless authentication, restrict device enrollment, and enforce Windows LAPS for automated local admin password rotation.

strategies.name: Endpoint Protection (09.x)
strategies.description: Controls for securing endpoints through device compliance baselines, configuration management, endpoint detection and response, and advanced threat protection. Covers Intune device policies, Defender for Endpoint, and attack surface reduction.

ML1.summary: Define device compliance baselines across all platforms and deploy core endpoint detection: enforce BitLocker, Secure Boot, TPM, minimum OS versions, and enable Defender for Endpoint EDR with antivirus and next-generation protection.

ML2.summary: Harden endpoint configuration and enhance detection: deploy Defender AV policies, Windows update rings, mobile app protection, CIS security baselines, Edge browser hardening, firewall policies, vulnerability management, web content filtering, and automated investigation.

ML3.summary: Implement advanced endpoint hardening and threat response: deploy attack surface reduction rules, Credential Guard, diagnostic data restrictions, exploit protection, controlled folder access, removable storage control, device control, application guard, and advanced hunting.

strategies.name: Transmission Protection (10.x)
strategies.description: Controls for protecting information in transit through email security, anti-phishing, anti-malware, and safe messaging policies. Covers Exchange Online transport rules, Defender for Office 365, DKIM/DMARC authentication, and URL/attachment scanning.

ML1.summary: Establish communications security: enforce TLS for Exchange transport, configure DKIM/DMARC email authentication, block auto-forwarding to external domains, and deploy baseline anti-phishing policies.

ML2.summary: Strengthen email and messaging security: enable mailbox auditing, deploy DKIM signing, configure anti-spoofing, Safe Links URL scanning, Safe Attachments sandboxing, and impersonation protection policies.

ML3.summary: Implement advanced communications protection: disable external calendar sharing, configure mail flow rules for sensitive content, deploy tenant allow/block lists, and advanced Safe Links/Attachments with zero-hour auto-purge.

strategies.name: Audit Logging & Monitoring (12.x)
strategies.description: Controls ensuring organizational activities are auditable and that audit records are generated, reviewed, and retained. Covers unified audit logging, Purview Audit Premium, communication compliance, and insider risk monitoring.

ML1.summary: Enable foundational audit capabilities: activate unified audit logging across all M365 workloads and deploy Purview Audit standard policies for regulatory monitoring and compliance evidence collection.

ML2.summary: Extend audit and incident coverage: deploy DLP incident management and eDiscovery hold policies for legal preservation and enhanced event capture across workloads.

ML3.summary: Implement advanced compliance monitoring: deploy insider risk investigation policies and communication compliance monitoring for data exfiltration detection and regulatory surveillance.

strategies.name: Data Protection & Privacy (06.x, 07.x)
strategies.description: Controls for protecting information at rest through data classification, sensitivity labelling, data loss prevention, encryption, and SharePoint/OneDrive sharing and access governance. Covers Purview Information Protection, DLP policies, and site-level controls.

ML1.summary: Establish data classification foundations: deploy sensitivity labels, configure DLP policies for credit card and personal data detection, enforce BitLocker encryption, and set baseline SharePoint sharing and access restrictions.

ML2.summary: Extend data protection: deploy sensitivity label auto-labelling, encryption-enforcing labels, DLP for Exchange/Teams/SharePoint, endpoint DLP, exact data matching, and granular SharePoint sharing restrictions with data access governance.

ML3.summary: Implement comprehensive data controls: deploy advanced DLP tuning, data lifecycle management, retention policies across workloads, and strict SharePoint site-level access controls, versioning, and advanced classification policies.

strategies.name: Business Continuity (17.x)
strategies.description: Controls for preparing for, responding to, and recovering from disruptions. Covers Teams meeting and collaboration policies, retention and recovery controls, and continuity of operations to ensure system availability.

ML1.summary: Establish collaboration and continuity foundations: configure Teams meeting policies to prevent anonymous join and lobby bypass, enforce meeting recording consent, and restrict external domain access.

ML2.summary: Strengthen collaboration security: restrict external messaging, disable unmanaged file sharing in Teams chats, control meeting chat and file upload capabilities, and enforce channel-level policies.

ML3.summary: Implement advanced collaboration controls: restrict external app and cloud storage access in Teams, enforce meeting watermarks, disable email-to-channel functionality, and restrict channel creation permissions.
